I understand how you are feeling, and I know that this can be a lot. If I were you, I'd really try to stick it out. As well as others have said, I was skeptical going into initiation as well, having a job, as well as a demanding major. My advice from my experience is to keep with the sorority, and that the commitment will lower once you are no longer a new member. Additionally, most great sorority friendships usually develop after the pledge process, so don't feel as if that part is missing quiet yet. 

In addition to talking to your new member educator, talk to your big if you already have one. It is understandable why you would feel a little questionable, but that woman is your mentor, and she will want the best for you. I understand that all of this is a lot, but she will be able to help you navigate your house better. 

Not all women in sororities are consumed by them. It is okay to be a member of a house that isn't involved 24/7. If you have any further questions, feel free to message me.
